correctness.rationale: Cauchy facet projection yields B_d(U)=E_sign|sign·U| with the 2^{d−1}/(d−1)! normalization. Rotational symmetry gives mean √d Γ(d/2)/(√πΓ((d+1)/2)); the normalized inner product of two independent sign vectors is 1−2K/d, K∼Bin(d,1/2). The bivariate Gaussian absolute-product identity produces E B²=(2/π)E f(1−2K/d). Independent exact Rademacher moments through degree six, Taylor coefficients 1/2,1/24,1/80 of f, and gamma Stirling expansion exhibit cancellation at orders d^0,d^{-1},d^{-2} and surviving 1/(3π)d^{-3}. Numerically evaluating the exact formula up to d=512 gives d³ variance 0.106394 versus 0.106103 target. Hoeffding tails justify truncation for the unbounded integer limit; finite numerics do not substitute for it.

originality.rationale: The full-text Kabluchko–Litvak–Zaporozhets result computes moments of one-dimensional projected width; this problem measures (d−1)-dimensional hyperplane projection volume (brightness) and thus is not implied by those line-width formulas. Horváth–Lángi provide the volume-of-hull translation identity, and Ivanov studies projection extrema rather than the uniform second moment and third-order variance constant. The specific binomial brightness law and 1/(3π) asymptotic remain best-of-knowledge not covered.
residual_risks: Older stochastic-geometry literature may contain a general spherical second-moment brightness tensor whose cross-polytope specialization yields the finite formula.
No central limit theorem, whole-distribution concentration bound, or arbitrary-axis theorem is implied by the variance asymptotic.

value.rationale: Sharp d^{-3} variance, with two nontrivial cancellations, quantifies concentration of random hyperplane shadows of a canonical high-dimensional polytope. It answers an intrinsic geometric probability question beyond merely evaluating the mean, and the exact binomial expression supports future fluctuation analysis.

final_claim: For uniform random hyperplane normals of the standard d-dimensional cross-polytope, the all-dimensional normalized brightness first two moments have the stated gamma/binomial formulas and d^3 Var(B_d)→1/(3π).
limitations: Only standard equal-axis cross-polytopes and uniform hyperplane directions.
Asymptotic variance is not a distributional limit theorem.
